clue.text: Reprimand for appearing in casual clothes

definitions.meaning: wearing less formal clothing than usual, as on an office's relaxed day

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded for turning up to work dressed too casually.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: a scolding, and the practice of wearing informal garments.

clue.text: Killed a medico and confessed

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for a doctor, a medico
to own up or own to something is to confess it

explanation.surface: A doctor kills someone and then admits to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To die by suffocation in water is to be killed in that particular way, a past participle like the definition.

clue.text: Scoff about the hundred pounds required to see show

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round the others

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about having to pay a hundred pounds for a theatre ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: Showiness or ostentatious brilliance is the sense of this borrowed French word, as in done with great flourish.

clue.text: Cut and then join together one by one

parts.note: to sever is to cut
to ally is to unite or join together

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut something and then rejoin the pieces singly.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means separately or individually, each in turn.

clue.text: Time for reflection just the same

indicators.note: the word reads identically when mirrored, back to front, so the answer is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A moment set aside for quiet thought which turns out unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a time of day, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Realise the record's come to an end?

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record; the 's is 'is', taken as a link
something finished is over

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the record has finished playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out or become aware of something is a synonym for come to realise it.

clue.text: Sewer-contaminated river

indicators.note: contaminated suggests the letters of the word are spoilt and mixed up

explanation.surface: A river polluted by sewage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weser is a river in northern Germany, flowing to the North Sea at Bremerhaven.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a German waterway flowing past Bremen.

clue.text: Talk, being contrary

definitions.meaning: to chat or hold a conversation

explanation.surface: Someone who argues just to be awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to chat; as an adjective it means opposite or reversed in order.

clue.text: A floor of stone in accommodation fit only for pigs

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a pen for pigs
ore is rock or mineral from which metal is extracted, loosely stone

explanation.surface: A stone floor in a squalid dwelling fit only for pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: One level of a building is a synonym for a floor.

clue.text: About fifty-one, plain but not at all concerned

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the plain word wraps the number

parts.note: obvious means plain, clear to see
LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone aged about fifty-one, plain-looking but unbothered.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaware and heedless; someone with no concern for what goes on around them.

clue.text: Momentary fault in electrical equipment

definitions.meaning: a ... circuit, where current bypasses its intended path

explanation.surface: A brief glitch in an electrical appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief in duration, and the everyday shortening of short circuit.

clue.text: A public official's try-on — a misrepresentation

indicators.note: a misrepresentation presents the letters in a false form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A civil servant's attempted deception, a false account.
explanation.walkthrough: A try-on is British slang for an attempt to deceive. 'misrepresentation' rearranges TRYON plus A; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal officer who witnesses signatures and certifies documents is a kind of public official.

clue.text: Kid heading for the water will take a turn at the wheel

definitions.text: will take a turn at the wheel

parts.note: to cod is British slang for to kid or hoax; heading for places it in front
a river is a stretch of water

explanation.surface: A young goat making for the river while someone else drives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' just places the kid in front of the water; COD is British slang for kid, to hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: A second driver who shares the driving takes turns steering.

clue.text: Very quiet in depression — it's spotted

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dale is a valley, a depression in the land
PP is pianissimo, the musical direction for very quiet

explanation.surface: Someone feeling very quiet and depressed is noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mottled marking or an animal with patches of colour: something that is spotted.

clue.text: Acquire some advantage

definitions.meaning: a grip or leverage, a hold giving some advantage

explanation.surface: Gaining some benefit from a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to buy; as a noun, a firm hold or leverage.

clue.text: Do without men

parts.note: reads as manage without males, but 'Do' is a party, and this is a women-only celebration before a wedding

explanation.surface: Getting by without any men around.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebration for a bride-to-be and her female friends is a party with no males.

clue.text: Handle fish on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the fish come first

parts.note: pike are freshwater fish
the Taff is a river in Wales flowing through Cardiff

explanation.surface: Picking up fish caught on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden shaft of a pike, a long pole, works as a handle.

clue.text: His word is law at a court function

indicators.note: function as an operation means the letters are processed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A grand event at a royal court where one person's word goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler whose every command must be obeyed.

clue.text: Clamour about a right to execute

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the clamour goes round the rest

parts.note: to cry out is to clamour

explanation.surface: An uproar about someone's right to execute a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform or accomplish a task, a phrasal synonym for execute.

clue.text: Wins over church members

parts.note: arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: A congregation is won over.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to win them over by delight; third person singular like the definition.

clue.text: A quick break, perhaps, for some of these winter sports enthusiasts

definitions.text: A quick break, perhaps, for some of these winter sports enthusiasts

parts.words: A quick break, perhaps, for some of these winter sports enthusiasts
parts.note: reads as a short holiday, but for some people on the slopes the break is a fractured leg from a fast run

explanation.surface: A short winter holiday for keen snow-sports fans.
explanation.definitionFit: People who slide down snowy slopes on long runners are winter sports enthusiasts.

clue.text: Toss the head, showing lack of confidence

parts.note: to shy is to throw or toss
a ness is a headland, a head of land

explanation.surface: Tossing one's head back, betraying nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Timidity, a reluctance to put oneself forward.

clue.text: Unhappily he said no steady attachment

indicators.note: unhappily suggests the letters are put out of their proper state and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone sadly refused a long-term relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticking fast to something is a firm, steady attachment.

clue.text: Children welcome visits from a social worker in South Africa

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an ant is a social insect, a worker in the colony

explanation.surface: Children are glad to see a visiting social worker in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a caseworker but a worker ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas, the gift-bringer whose Christmas Eve visits children look forward to.

clue.text: Great game for a high-flier!

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, great
prey is game, animals hunted

explanation.surface: Big game is ideal for an ambitious person.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish-eating hawk that soars high over water is a high-flier.

clue.text: A jolly fellow no longer up the pole — at sea

definitions.text: A jolly fellow no longer up the pole — at sea

parts.words: A jolly fellow no longer up the pole — at sea
parts.note: reads as a cheerful man who is no longer crazy and is confused, but the jolly fellow is the pirate flag, no longer flown from the mast at sea

explanation.surface: A cheerful man who has recovered his wits but is still bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the pole' is British slang for mad; here it is literally hoisted on a flagpole. The Jolly Roger is the skull-and-crossbones pirate flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The second word of the pirate flag's name; pirates no longer fly it.

clue.text: A bill to the queen for ornamental tree

parts.note: AC or a/c is the abbreviation for account, a bill
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An invoice is sent to the monarch for a decorative tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical name for maples, often grown for their decorative foliage.

clue.text: Such a worker can be so taken in by humanity

indicators.note: taken in by means placed inside the following piece

parts.note: man means humankind, humanity

explanation.surface: A labourer can be fooled by human nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder in stone is a kind of worker.

clue.text: Figure there are soldiers about to get involved

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers
C is the abbreviation for circa, about
to tangle with is to get involved

explanation.surface: A count of soldiers about to enter a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong shape with four right angles is a geometric figure.

clue.text: The degree of damage after a storm's apparent

indicators.note: damage suggests the letters are knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: The extent of destruction becomes clear once a storm has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: A postgraduate university qualification in the humanities is a degree.
